key_insight: MV-VDP uses a multi-view video diffusion policy to jointly model 3D spatial structure and temporal dynamics, enabling action generation that is aware of the environment's full spatio-temporal state.
problem_solved: Existing robotic policies often rely on 2D observations and image-pretrained backbones, missing 3D structure or temporal dynamics and demanding large amounts of data; MV-VDP addresses this by integrating multi-view inputs and temporal modeling into a single diffusion-based policy.
method: Condition a diffusion-based generative policy on synchronized multi-view video to capture multi-perspective spatial cues.
Learn a compact 3D spatio-temporal latent (implicit or voxel-aware) that encodes scene geometry and temporal evolution for downstream action generation.
Sample action or trajectory sequences by denoising in the learned latent space, training the policy end-to-end for robotic manipulation tasks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable way to incorporate 3D and temporal context into action policies, improving sample efficiency and robustness for real-world robotic manipulation and dynamic scene reasoning.
visual_elements: Multi-view camera grid feeding into a single model (illustrates inputs)
3D scene reconstruction/latent overlay with temporal trajectory arrows (shows spatio-temporal state)
Diffusion-denoising timeline from noisy latent to generated action sequence (explains method)
Bar chart comparing sample efficiency / task success vs. 2D-only baselines (quantitative impact)
paper_title: Multi-View Video Diffusion Policy: A 3D Spatio-Temporal-Aware Video Action Model
paper_authors: Peiyan Li, Yixiang Chen, Yuan Xu, Jiabing Yang, Xiangnan Wu
